groups.title: Restricted-use and general-use nounstems
groups.proposal: Keep one lexical nounstem record with the Andrews-authorized restricted-use and general-use forms needed by different constructions.
groups.writingJob: Use the restricted-use stem in an absolutive-state NNC and the general-use stem in a possessive-state NNC or compound embed position.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in recognizing which use-stem is present and why its shape may differ.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies or chooses the noun meaning; the application selects the required use-stem from the construction.
groups.controlPolicy: No restricted/general picker; construction and State determine the stem automatically.

groups.title: The four nounstem classes and their permitted shapes
groups.proposal: Store the nounstem's lexical class and authorized alternatives, then enforce the class-conditioned stem and connector possibilities without guessing class from spelling alone.
groups.writingJob: Build tl-, tli-, in-, and zero-class NNCs with their valid final shapes, supportive-vowel variants, alternative class memberships, and base, truncated, or glottalized general-use shapes.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in identifying class evidence while keeping lexical class membership and genuine alternative analyses open.
groups.decisionSplit: The user may enter any nounstem; the application uses known lexical class information or asks only when more than one class is genuinely possible and unresolved.
groups.controlPolicy: Class is normally an application obligation; expose a class choice only for unknown input or an Andrews-authorized alternative.

groups.title: Number, affinity, and distributive or varietal nounstems
groups.proposal: Keep grammatical number on the personal-pronoun subject while deriving affinity or distributive/varietal meaning inside the nounstem.
groups.writingJob: Form the long-vowel affinity reduplication or glottal-stop distributive/varietal reduplication from the source nounstem and preserve animate versus nonanimate applicability.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in distinguishing subject number from the nounstem's cohesive-group or separate-members meaning.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended relationship meaning when relevant; the application builds the correct reduplicated stem and keeps it separate from subject number.
groups.controlPolicy: Use a meaning-based plain, affinity, or distributive/varietal choice; never call it noun plural.

groups.title: Absolutive singular or common nounstem selection
groups.proposal: Use only the base shape of the restricted-use nounstem for an absolutive-state NNC with a singular or common-number subject.
groups.writingJob: Select the base restricted-use stem, preserve all four nounstem classes, and permit a derived distributive/varietal base when its meaning is intended.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in identifying the subject's singular/common number and the base nounstem independently.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses State, subject, and intended stem meaning; the application selects the base restricted-use shape.
groups.controlPolicy: No stem-shape control; reuse State, Subject, and the derived-stem meaning choice.

groups.title: Absolutive plural stem and connector selection
groups.proposal: Build plural-subject absolutive NNCs from the noun's authorized plain, affinity, or distributive/varietal stem and its lexical connector pattern.
groups.writingJob: Select t, m, or zero plus the proper number ending, enforce obligatory or preferred affinity forms, and preserve authorized alternatives without manufacturing them.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through lexical variation, preferred forms, and the difference between stem derivation and subject plurality.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the subject and intended relationship; the application selects known lexical forms, asking only when equally authorized alternatives remain a genuine choice.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not expose connector morphs; expose only a genuine authorized form choice when meaning and context do not settle it.

groups.title: Possessive plural nounstem selection
groups.proposal: Normally use the plain general-use stem for possessive plural NNCs, but use affinity or distributive/varietal stems when the intended relationship requires them.
groups.writingJob: Build the selected general-use nounstem with the possessive plural subject connector hu-ān.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in recognizing whether the nounstem adds cohesion, distribution, or variety to a plural possessive subject.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended relationship; the application supplies the general-use shape and possessive plural connector.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the relationship choice; do not add a connector or use-stem control.

groups.title: Possessive singular or common class subclasses
groups.proposal: Select the lexical class subclass, general-use stem shape, and subject connector required for a possessive singular/common NNC.
groups.writingJob: Build base or truncated general-use stems; select zero, hui, or uh; delete only ephemeral vowels; and add supportive i only when truncation creates an illegal cluster.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader in separating stem-final material from subject connectors and in recognizing ephemeral-vowel deletion and supportive-vowel repair.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the nounstem, possessor, and subject; the application performs all class, truncation, connector, and phonological work.
groups.controlPolicy: No subclass, truncation, connector, or supportive-i controls; lexical authority and grammar determine them.

groups.title: Ambiguous NNC constituent analysis
groups.proposal: Preserve all grammatically possible NNC analyses until vocabulary, morphs, sound changes, length, and typed source information settle the structure.
groups.writingJob: Generate from the typed structure without collapsing distinct stems or connectors that happen to have the same spelling.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through ambiguities involving uh, tl, tli, o, m, vowel length, glottal stop, and supportive i.
groups.decisionSplit: The application keeps structural possibilities open; the user is asked only for source meaning or structure that cannot be derived from the entered spelling.
groups.controlPolicy: Use one minimal Exception or analysis choice only when real ambiguity remains; never ask the user to choose a morph the application already knows.
